name: fix_node_url_query_parsing
description: Replaces naive query-string splitting with proper URL decoding
prompts: parseQuery in query.js hand-rolls query-string parsing with string splits: percent-encoded values stay encoded ('caf%C3%A9' instead of 'café'), '+' is not decoded to a space, values containing '=' get truncated, and a '#fragment' after the query leaks into the last value. Fix query.js using Node's built-in URL/URLSearchParams (parse relative URLs against a dummy base like 'http://x'), keeping the same contract: an object of decoded key -> value strings, later duplicate keys overwriting earlier ones, and '' for valueless keys.
